claim.quote: We report on the final electroweak measurements performed with data taken at the Z resonance by the experiments operating at the electron-positron colliders SLC and LEP.

date.note: arXiv submission month (7 Sep 2005); journal publication followed in 2006.

key_value_text.quote: The number of light neutrino species is determined to be 2.9840+/-0.0082.
key_value_text.value: The abstract says the mass and width of the Z boson and its couplings to fermions are precisely measured, and that the number of light neutrino species is determined to be 2.9840 ± 0.0082; it reports electroweak radiative corrections beyond the running of the QED and QCD couplings observed with a significance of five standard deviations, and the largest difference from the Standard Model expectation among Z-pole measurements, the b-quark forward-backward asymmetry, at 2.8 standard deviations.

name: Precision Electroweak Measurements on the Z Resonance
notes: SLD (SLC Large Detector) is one of the five contributing experiments/collaborations in this combination but is outside the scope of this workstream (not a CERN experiment) and is not listed in experiment_ids/collaboration_ids; only the four LEP experiments are recorded here.

summary.plain: The LEP and SLC collaborations combined their final measurements of the Z boson, from 17 million Z decays at LEP and 600 thousand at SLC, and compared them with the Standard Model. The paper reports that the largest difference from the Standard Model expectation among the Z-pole measurements is 2.8 standard deviations, in the b-quark forward-backward asymmetry.
summary.technical: ALEPH, DELPHI, L3, OPAL and SLD combination (Phys. Rept. 427, 2006, 257-454; arXiv:hep-ex/0509008): 17 million Z decays accumulated by ALEPH, DELPHI, L3 and OPAL at LEP and 600 thousand by SLD at SLC; cross-sections, forward-backward and polarised asymmetries; Z mass and width and couplings to fermions precisely measured; number of light neutrino species 2.9840 ± 0.0082. Electroweak radiative corrections beyond the running of the QED and QCD coupling constants are observed with a significance of five standard deviations and in agreement with the Standard Model; the largest Z-pole difference from the Standard Model expectation is the b-quark forward-backward asymmetry, at 2.8 standard deviations.

title: Precision Electroweak Measurements on the Z Resonance
why_it_matters: The abstract says the results are compared to the predictions of the Standard Model, that the top-quark and W-boson masses predicted through radiative corrections are compared to the direct measurements, and that this provides a stringent test of the Standard Model.
